Refactor image building - Scaling algorithm is matched with Deptcharge's: square drawing area in the center, per-image scaling parameters, integer divisions. This will prevent Depthcharge from rendering blurry images on the default display by scaling. - Stretched screens are detected by comparing aspect ratio of 'screen' and 'panel'. If it's stretched, images are squeezed so that final result will look proportional on display. - Removed max_size_limit. It's meaningless now because images are compressed when written to the flash image. - Use only PNG as a source for all images (texts and assets) - Use only assets2x - Move dividers to assets2x dir - Remove background & dummy image - Remove make_default_yaml.py (which produces DEFAULT.yaml) - Use _DEFAULT_ to keep default values in boards.yaml - Increases font DPI from 90 to 180. 360 won't fit in the current boards' ROM (and has no visible advantage). 'hi_res' option in boards.yaml is used to specify locales whose text images will be rendered at a higher DPI. Otherwise, all locales are rendered in higher DPI by default. rockchip: spi: Set rxd sample delay when using high speed At higher SPI bus speeds the SPI RX value is not available in time for sampling at the normal time. Add a delay to ensure that we read the correct data. The value of 40ns is chosen arbitrarily. In my testing I can use a sample delay of 1 even at 24MHz. But since it is not necessary, I have left that case alone. It kicks in at 25MHz and up. cgpt: add support for managing the legacy boot gpt bit Bit 2 in the GPT partition attributes has been allocated as the legacy bios boot (equivalent to the "active" or "boot" flag in MBR). If we try to boot images on newer x86 systems, syslinux dies because it can't find any GPT partition marked bootable. Update the various parts of cgpt add & show to manage this bit. Now we can run: cgpt add -i 12 -B 1 chromiumos_image.bin And the EFI partition will be marked bootable. cros_build_lib.py: tolerate tar modification check failure The tar program exits with code 1 if (and only if) it detects that the modification time of the file or directory it is archiving changes between the beginning and the end of reading it. Thus if, for instance, a temporary file is created and removed, the check will fail for that directory. This can catch valid races but can also produce spurious errors. We are too chicken to ignore these errors (perhaps rightfully so), so we try again but only once. (Note that check isn't offering reliable protection. The modification can happen after tar has processed the file or directory, in which case it goes unnoticed. A separate strategy is needed to isolate and fix this problem.) Introduce protected member for Service auto connect cooldown max Commit 0801d19 ("Throttle AutoConnect calls") introduces a cooldown timeout max of 30 minutes for all services in order to avoid a busy cycle that occurs on cellular devices when Service::Connect fails. This poses a problem for jetstream routers that are unable to acquire dhcp leases due to a downed ISP server as they become defunct for 30 minutes and require a power cycle. This change modifies the default timeout for all services to be 1 minute and introduces a protected member, max_auto_connect_cooldown_time_milliseconds_, which is overridden to be the previous 30 minute value for cellular services only. BUG=b:27207845 TEST=Added log to Service::ThrottleFutureAutoConnects and verified that net.log shows values reaching up to 1 minute on veyron_minnie-cheets. To test the cellular case, added conditional log to Service::ThrottleFutureAutoConnects and verified that max cooldown is set to the original 30 minutes on a link.
